newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up on improved economic data.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up on improved economic data.

text.p: Late bargain hunting sparked by welcome economic indicators released by the central bank helped push Thai stocks up at the close, brokers said.
The SET index, which had fallen in the past five consecutive trading days, finished 4.22 points higher to 910.33 on 3.4 billion baht turnover.

"Investors, mainly locals, bought finance and some bank issues before the market closed. They believed that the overall economic indicators, except the trade deficit, were good," Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities said.
The Bank of Thailand said on Thursday that Thailand's August trade deficit widened to 36.8 billion baht from a revised 35.5 billion in July.
But the current account deficit narrowed to 29.3 billion baht from 31.0 billion baht in the same period.

Brokers said the market whose blue-chip SET-50 index rose 0.42 point to 68.63 was also helped when one of the market support funds, run either by the private sector or the government, bought blue chip stocks, especially finance and banking counters.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, gaining two baht to 141. Large capitalised Finance One rose 1.50 to 59 and Krung Thai Bank also gained 1.50 to 70.
Brokers said the index is expected to move in narrow range tomorrow. Support is seen at 896 while resistance at 920.
